effects.log: You walk out together. Halfway home {npc} asks if it matters. You say it matters less than {he} thinks.

choices.text: Ask the diviner what can be done

effects.log: The diviner says some roots wake late, and some never. Neither of you is comforted.

effects.log: The whole house wakes up to see what the noise is. Then the whole house is laughing.

events.text: The examination lists are posted in the provincial capital, and {npc}'s name is on them. A rootless child of a martial house, and now an official of the empire, with a seal and a hat to prove it.

effects.log: The whole street eats. The martial houses who laughed at the root test send gifts, a little late.

effects.log: {npc} agrees, and mentions that you will need to fill in the forms properly from now on.

events.text: The child is called {npc}, a prodigy of another family, the pride of a house that has done you no harm. You have found where {he} sleeps. What you would do there is not a thing to be told. It is still not too late to turn the horse around.

choices.text: Do it. Your child will have a future

effects.log: You come home before dawn and do not speak of where you were. Something in you does not come home with you.
You turn the horse. Your child will have to find another road, and you will have to help. It is the harder road. It is the right one.

events.text: A demonic healer told you it could be done: a root moved from one child to another, if the other is young and strong. The healer named a child, {npc}, of a family three valleys away. You are outside their wall now. Nobody would ever know. Except you.

effects.log: It is done. The healer is paid. You wash your hands three times and they never feel clean again.
You go home and sit with your own child until morning. The healer's silver stays in your purse.

events.text: A traveller at the inn mentions a family three valleys over whose prodigy lost {his} root in one night, and a parent, {npc}, who has sold the family fields to pay for questions. The questions are about you.

effects.log: You sharpen your blade and sleep lighter. They will come.

choices.text: Send {npc} silver, unsigned, as a blood-price

effects.log: The silver is sent back, and then, a month later, taken after all. The questions stop. The hate does not, but it stays home.

events.text: {npc} came for your child on the road, not for you. Your people got there in time, mostly. Your child is hurt and will mend, and knows now that somebody hates them enough to try. The root you gave them is still there.

choices.text: Tell your child the truth at last

effects.log: Your child listens to all of it and then leaves the room without a word. They come back three days later. Not the same.

choices.text: Hunt {npc} down before the next try

effects.log: You go looking. {npc} has gone to ground. Next time it will be you {he} comes for.

events.text: {npc} stands at your gate in broad day with a drawn sword and every neighbour watching. "My child had a future," {he} says. "You gave it to yours." There is no way out of this but through it.

ok.log: You win. You let {npc} live. {He} walks away with nothing left but the knowing, and so do you.

fail.log: You lose, and {npc} stands over you and does not finish it. "Live with it," {he} says, and goes.

choices.text: Kneel and offer everything you can pay

effects.log: You kneel in your own gateway in front of the whole street. {npc} takes the silver and spits at your feet. It ends.

events.text: The first court of your new kingdom meets in a hall that was a granary last month. There are more petitions than chairs. A farmer wants a bridge, a captain wants pay, a scholar wants to write the laws. Everyone wants to see what kind of ruler you are.

effects.log: The bridge goes up by harvest. The farmers remember who built it.
The army cheers you at the next muster. The farmers wait, and notice.

choices.text: Let the scholar write the laws

effects.log: The laws are long and fair and nobody reads them. They hold anyway.

events.text: An envoy of the Emperor arrives in silk, with a hundred riders and a scroll: the throne will forgive your kingdom if you kneel, pay tribute and call yourself its servant. The scroll does not say what happens if you do not.

effects.log: You kneel. The envoy smiles. Your court watches, and some of them remember.

choices.text: Send the envoy home with a gift and no answer

effects.log: The envoy goes. The answer that is not an answer travels ahead of the envoy.

choices.text: Tear up the scroll in front of the court

effects.log: Your court roars. Somewhere to the east an army begins to gather.

events.text: An army is on the border: the Emperor's, or a neighbour who thinks a new kingdom is an easy one. Your generals spread the maps and wait for you to speak.

ok.log: You ride at the front. The enemy breaks at the river. Your kingdom is larger by a valley.

fail.log: The line breaks. You are carried off the field. The kingdom loses two towns before the peace.

choices.text: Hold the walls and wait them out

effects.log: The siege lasts a season. The enemy goes home hungry. So does everyone else.
The army turns around. Your treasury is lighter and your borders the same.

events.text: The rains did not come. The granaries of your kingdom are half empty by midwinter and the roads are full of families walking south.

effects.log: Nobody starves. The families walk back north in spring, and they talk about you on the way.

choices.text: Keep the grain for the army

effects.log: The army eats. The villages do not forget.

events.text: Your ministers have split into two camps: the old captains who fought for your banner, and the new scholars who run your treasury. Each brings you a list of the other's crimes.

effects.log: Three scholars are sent home. The ledgers get worse within a year.
The captains grumble into their wine. The ledgers balance for the first time.
Both camps are furious with you, which is the same as being at peace.

events.text: Envoys from two neighbouring kingdoms arrive in the same week, each offering an alliance against the other. Both brought gifts. Both brought a list of what they want.

effects.log: The treaty is signed in red ink. The weaker neighbour sends no more envoys.
Both envoys go home sure they have won. Your treasury is the only one that has.

choices.text: Refuse both: your kingdom stands alone

effects.log: Your court thinks it bold. Your generals think it expensive. Both are right.

events.text: A magistrate of your kingdom is caught taking bribes from the salt merchants. They are also the best magistrate you have. The whole court waits to see what kind of law your kingdom keeps.

choices.text: Dismiss and punish them in public

effects.log: The salt price drops within a month. The other magistrates count their silver more carefully.

choices.text: Fine them quietly and keep them

effects.log: The salt merchants learn the price of your favour. So does everyone else.

events.text: Locusts. They come over the hills in a cloud that darkens noon, and when they leave the river valley of your kingdom is bare to the root.

choices.text: Buy grain from abroad at any price

effects.log: The grain barges come up the river by autumn. The valley eats, and remembers whose barges they were.

choices.text: Order the army to plant and dig

effects.log: Soldiers in the fields grumble and dig. The second harvest is thin, but it is a harvest.

choices.text: Wait it out behind the walls

effects.log: The capital eats. The valley does not, and the valley does not forget.

events.text: The village bully's father, a burly third-rate fighter, comes to your door to complain that you hit the boy back. {npc} listens politely, very politely, and something in the yard goes very still. The man's teacup cracks in a clenched fist.

choices.text: Say nothing: you will handle it yourself

effects.log: {npc} apologises for the cracked cup and pours the visitor another. You work out your own way with the bully. It takes a while.

choices.text: Look at {npc} and ask what just happened

effects.log: {npc} says the cup was old. The bully's father is telling the whole village otherwise by evening.

events.text: A sect recruiter passing through laughs at your forms in the village square and says no child of a farming family will ever amount to anything. {npc} walks over. The recruiter stops laughing, and then cannot quite remember why.

choices.text: Say nothing: you will handle it yourself

effects.log: {npc} only asks the recruiter for directions, and the moment passes. You practise twice as hard that winter, out of spite.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what was said to the recruiter

effects.log: {npc} says it was the weather. The recruiter left town before dawn, and the story is everywhere.

events.arc: A Parent Who Hides Their Peak

events.text: Men on the road take you for ransom and tie you in a cart. That night the cart stops. There is one sound, very short, and then {npc} is untying you, not out of breath, the men asleep in a neat row by the road.

choices.text: Say nothing: you will handle it yourself

effects.log: {npc} says they must have been half asleep. You decide to believe it, and to learn to untie your own knots.
{npc} sighs, the long sigh of someone who has been waiting for this question for years.

events.text: {npc} closes the door, sits you down and stops pretending. The pressure of {his} qi fills the room like deep water. "I left all that behind for a quiet life," {he} says. "But you are going out into it whether I like it or not."

mem.note: told me the truth at last

effects.log: The lessons start before dawn the next day and do not stop.
It is a long story, with a sect, a war and a grave in it. You understand {npc} better at the end of it.

events.text: The house's drill master wakes you before the birds, every day, with cold water. You run the walls with stones on your back while {npc}, the heir, watches from a window with a bowl of rice porridge.

choices.text: Run until you drop, and get up

effects.log: You drop three times. The drill master writes something in a little book each time you get up.

mem.note: waved at me from the wall

effects.log: {npc} waves back, then looks around to see if anyone saw.

events.text: {npc} finds you in the stables after a beating from the drill master and sits down beside you in the straw. "They tell me you would die for me," {he} says. "Would you? Truly?"

choices.text: "Yes. Because you asked, not because they told me."

effects.log: {npc} does not say anything for a long time. Then {he} shares the sweets {he} brought.

choices.text: "That is what I was bought for."

effects.log: {npc} goes very red, and leaves the sweets anyway.

events.text: An assassin in the night market, a knife meant for {npc}. You are between them before you have decided to be. The knife finds your arm instead. The house surgeon says it will heal. The house says this is what you are for.

mem.note: took the knife meant for me

effects.log: You do not make a sound while it is stitched. {npc} holds your other hand and does.

choices.text: Ask the house for a reward

effects.log: The steward pays, as for a broken tool mended. {npc} watches, and something in {his} face shuts.

events.text: You are eighteen. The house that bought you off the street asks you to swear the blade-oath to {npc}: for life, in front of the ancestors. The gate stands open behind you. Nobody is guarding it. They have never had to.

effects.log: You swear. {npc} swears something back that is not in any rite. The ancestors do not object.

choices.text: Walk out of the open gate

effects.log: Nobody stops you. A blade that walks away on its own is not a blade any more. It is a person.

choices.text: Turn the blade on the house that made you

effects.log: You leave the hall in an uproar and the oath unsworn. The house will remember you as its worst mistake.
